title: B07 layout re-verification and B08 dark theme
method: The card was measured through its real root ([data-openui-card]). An earlier attempt walked up from the Button and landed on a transparent wrapper, which would have let an unstyled card pass; that mistake is why the first B07 measurement reported a healthy card that the screenshot contradicted.
Layout acceptance is numeric: every leaf node left edge must equal the card content left edge within 1px, and a Button must not span the content width.

Theme acceptance is numeric: every bridged CSS variable must resolve, and every text/background pair must clear WCAG AA 4.5:1 for body text, measured against the nearest ancestor that actually paints a background.
Both schemes were switched through the host's own Settings > 通用设置 > 外观 control, so the theme change is the host's, not a class the probe added.

B07.note: Every leaf sits at leftOffset 0 and the Button keeps its own 88.8px width instead of stretching.

B08.note: The light button pair (4.23:1) is the host's own: the DSH send button and the "1017" badge use the identical #4176e6/#fff pairing. Dark measures 5.61:1.

defects.summary: Every CSS variable the OpenUI card referenced resolved to empty, so the whole component table rendered unstyled: a Button with no background, no border and square corners.
defects.evidence: probes/var-resolution.mjs: 0 of 12 declared variables resolved. Screenshot screenshots/b07-before-themefix.png shows the result.
defects.rootCause: The card used the frame-CSS vocabulary (--foreground, --primary, --border, --radius, --font-sans), which the HTML backend declares inside its own iframe document. A host-mounted card has no such document, and DSH publishes its palette only as --dsw-alias-* and --dsw-static-* tokens (458 custom properties on the card, none of them named --foreground). A var() that does not resolve is invalid at computed-value time, so every declaration using one fell back to its initial value.
defects.fix: OpenUICard.tsx declares a HOST_TOKENS bridge on the card root, mapping each frame variable to its host token with a literal fallback, reusing the same token names theme.ts already established for the HTML backend.
defects.lesson: The card had rendered "correctly" in the stage-1.2 screenshot because text inherits colour from the chat; only a screenshot showed the missing button, and only a computed-style probe explained it.

defects.summary: The Button set a `border` shorthand alongside a borderColor longhand from its variant table, so border-width and border-style resolved to nothing.
defects.evidence: Computed border came back as "0px none rgb(15,17,21)" while the inline style listed empty border-top-style and border-top-width longhands.
defects.fix: Use borderWidth / borderStyle / borderColor longhands consistently, in both the base rule and BUTTON_KINDS.

defects.summary: The primary Button failed WCAG AA in dark mode: #353638 on #5686fe measured 3.59:1.
defects.rootCause: --primary-foreground was bridged to --dsw-alias-label-primary-inverted, which the host does not pair with its brand fill. In dark mode that token is #353638, a dark grey, because "inverted" there means inverted against the page, not against the accent.
defects.fix: Bridge to --dsw-alias-label-primary-foreground instead, the token the host itself pairs with a filled brand surface. Measures 5.61:1 on the dark brand and 5.61:1 on the light brand.

defects.summary: The two backends disagreed about what a card title looks like, and the OpenUI one put it below AA.
defects.evidence: The HTML card title measured 18.9:1; the OpenUI card title measured 2.13:1 using the caption tier.
defects.fix: Use the same treatment as VisualizeCard.tsx: foreground ink at 0.65 opacity. --muted-foreground also moved from the caption tier (2.13:1) to the tertiary tier (3.71:1), the one the host uses for its own small meta text.
defects.note: The caption tier is a host-wide choice, not something this plugin introduced: the host paints its own "High" label in the same 2.13:1 colour. The card no longer adds to it.

defects.summary: The semantic colour names in the component table were offset by one against the series palette: success pointed at amber, warning at green, danger at purple.
defects.fix: Realigned COLOR_VARS with the series order frame-css.ts uses, so one colour name means the same colour in both backends.

newTests: tests/openui-card.spec.tsx: declares every variable the component table references (renders OpenUICard and asserts the bridge is on the card root, because a var() only resolves against the element or an ancestor).
tests/openui-card.spec.tsx: keeps the semantic colour names on their own series.
tests/openui-card.spec.tsx: gives a Button a real border rather than a shorthand conflict.
conclusion: B07 and B08 are closed with browser evidence, not unit tests. Closing them exposed five further defects that the stage-1.2 record had marked as a styling detail: the OpenUI card was rendering with no CSS variables resolved at all.
